Monica — quick technical notes based on the pilot configuration they demoed: 

- Model request flow: customer requests hit EU front-ends (we have edge ingress in frankfurt and london). Live inference is routed to either EU or US GPU pools based on account routing policy. For Meditrek we can pin to EU-only serving nodes for the pilot.
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral by design; default TTL 30s for inference cache entries. We do not persist client prompts to long-term stores by default.
- Logs & telemetry: request-level telemetry and aggregated metrics are currently stored in us-east-1 for analytics (30d retention). We can provide a scoped export of telemetry that excludes prompt content and push a region-restricted copy on request (will require a config change and Ops runbook).
- Subprocessors: attached is the latest map with roles and regions. Note that our observability vendor (LogSight) processes aggregated traces and is US-based; they do not routinely have access to full request payloads, but we will confirm contractual limits.

I attached subprocessors_map_v2.csv with fields: name, role, primary-region, access-to-cleartext (yes/no). Short answer: we can provide SCCs and coordinate a UK IDTA path, but Legal will need to sign off on the exact carveouts (especially telemetry storage).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm pilot config: EU-only serving and logs redaction enabled.
2) Ops ticket to generate region-restricted telemetry copy + attestations.
3) Legal to review UK IDTA readiness — I flagged KMS/HSM stuff below for Vivek.

Attachment: subprocessors_map_v2.csv (text/csv)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Routing & transfer confirmations needed for Meditrek pilot — legal check

Thanks — reviewed the request. High-level legal position and required asks: 

- UK IDTA: For standard pilot workloads we can sign the UK IDTA with Meditrek subject to (A) confirmation that encrypted keys are customer-controlled where required, and (B) acceptable incident notification timelines (we propose 72 hours for security incidents). I have a redline prepared that narrows the telemetry carveout — see attached (UK_IDTA_template_redline.docx).
- SCCs: We can also offer the EU SCCs as an alternative; operationally that is similar but the customer often prefers the IDTA for UK-specific requirements. We should not dual-sign both unless Contracts approves.
- TIA: We'll need a scoped TIA for the pilot that covers data categories, data flows, subprocessor access levels, and retention. I can draft the TIA (short form) if Ops/Infra confirm EU-only serving and telemetry redaction.

Risks to call out to the customer explicitly: aggregated telemetry stored in us-east-1 (unless we deliver a region-limited export), and our observability vendor's access level. If Meditrek requires absolute assurance that no telemetry leaves the EEA/UK, we must run an Ops change and the lead time is 3-5 business days to stand up the export + attestations.

Suggested reply to Meditrek: propose a joint call to confirm pilot config and then deliver: (1) subprocessors map, (2) shortform TIA draft, (3) UK IDTA redline and signing path or SCC alternative.

Attachment: UK_IDTA_template_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
